target.title: Hatching assistant hangs after purpose when using OpenAI 5.5
target.body:
Related: problem-mode user report; no public issue number

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS onboarding/web chat using a short request deadline as the actual assistant run budget. With slower first replies, such as a newly configured OpenAI 5.5 session, the macOS hatch/chat path could appear stuck or time out before the assistant run should have been considered done.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Split the macOS `chat.send` run budget from the WebSocket ACK/request wait.
- Keep the ACK wait short at 30 seconds so an unreachable gateway still fails promptly.
- Send a five-minute `timeoutMs` for the assistant run and use the same five-minute budget for shared chat UI pending-run completion.
- Treat non-terminal `chat.send` acknowledgements such as `started` as pending until `agent.wait` or a final chat event completes the run.
- Did not change gateway protocol shape, provider routing, auth, model catalog behavior, session storage, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant get the same first-run-sized wait window used by terminal hatch. A slow first reply should remain pending instead of being treated as stuck or timed out after the old shorter macOS/shared chat budgets.

## Evidence

- Branch base checked during freshness gate: `main@ff1e7e1305cc63f6a5d9aba73426cabf4861a24f`. No final rebase was performed.
- Final branch head used for local validation: `ce11c8d748`.
- Real environment tested: macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Swift 6.3.3, Node v24.15.0, pnpm 11.2.2.

### Real macOS behavior proof

I launched the packaged macOS OpenClaw app in attach-only chat mode against a local proof gateway that accepts `chat.send`, returns a non-terminal `started` ACK, waits 70 seconds before completing `agent.wait`, then emits the final assistant reply. This exercises the real macOS app, WebSocket client, shared chat view model, and SwiftUI chat window across the old 30-second boundary.

Gateway request/timeout evidence from the proof run:

```text
2026-07-01T14:51:07.532Z [proof] chat.send timeoutMs=300000 requestAck=started runId=792ACA57-C94F-44C6-A7A3-7CB7FBB0CE65
2026-07-01T14:51:07.554Z [proof] agent.wait timeoutMs=300000 runId=792ACA57-C94F-44C6-A7A3-7CB7FBB0CE65 delaying=70000ms
2026-07-01T14:52:17.556Z [proof] agent.wait completed runId=792ACA57-C94F-44C6-A7A3-7CB7FBB0CE65
```

UI state before the delayed completion, 67 seconds after send and still before the 70-second assistant final:

```text
pending-capture-utc 2026-07-01T14:52:14Z
AX snapshot contained:
static text proof delayed response 70s
static text Gateway connected
Observed: the user message was visible, the gateway stayed connected, and the delayed assistant reply was not shown yet.
```

UI state after the delayed completion:

```text
completion-capture-utc 2026-07-01T14:55:53Z
AX snapshot contained:
static text proof delayed response 70s
static text Delayed assistant reply completed after 70000ms.
static text Gateway connected
Observed: the assistant reply appeared after completion and the pending run cleared.
```

This proves the macOS chat path no longer treats the short WebSocket ACK wait as the assistant run timeout: `chat.send.timeoutMs` and `agent.wait.timeoutMs` both used 300000 ms while a 70-second delayed run stayed pending and then completed.

### Local regression checks

```text
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests
-> pass, 81 tests in 1 suite

DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayConnectionControlTests
-> pass, 6 tests in 1 suite

pnpm format:swift
-> pass, 0/256 files require formatting, 4 files skipped

git diff --check
-> pass with no output

DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer pnpm lint:swift
-> macOS: 11 warnings, 0 serious in 256 files
-> iOS/shared: 6 warnings, 0 serious in 135 files
```

### GitHub checks after final push

```text
macos-swift -> pass, 2m1s
macos-node -> pass, 37s
Real behavior proof -> pass, 12s
ios-build -> pass, 1m18s
android-build-play -> pass, 3m51s
android-test-play -> pass, 2m23s
android-test-third-party -> pass, 2m13s
native-i18n -> pass, 34s
check-docs -> pass, 58s
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Swift regression tests plus real macOS app proof.
- Target test files: `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift` and `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Scenario locked in: default macOS chat send carries a 300000 ms run timeout, `agent.wait` receives the same timeout for completion, shared chat completion wait uses 300000 ms, and non-terminal `started` ACKs remain pending until completion.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the assertions sit at the two affected client boundaries: outgoing macOS gateway payloads and shared chat UI completion waiting.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: macOS chat used one 30-second value for two lifecycle layers: the quick WebSocket request wait and the actual assistant run budget. Shared chat UI pending state also used a shorter 120-second timeout.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no regression asserted the macOS `chat.send.timeoutMs` payload, `agent.wait.timeoutMs` payload, or shared chat completion wait against the five-minute first-run hatch budget.
